additional_concerns: Candidates node.1bf6918f69c6b37738daeb83, node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e, node.ce439b1cf9ed8301fbb68f94 and node.ea4d19630f8cab09065b1909 treat preserved legacy processing as an exclusion from relief. The circular expressly preserves processing but does not expressly establish that substantive exclusion. The proposed interpretation remains unresolved, especially after a later decision, withdrawal or resubmission.

Candidate node.4d548f2e09bc36ef51212f64 places legacy applications outside scope. Its OUT_OF_SCOPE result must not be interpreted as denial of relief. Candidate node.b66b3e831bb98a12db59dffa deliberately determines only substantive qualification.

The specified Effective Date supports commencement on 28 November 2025. Its relationship to the introductory immediate-effect wording and the legally relevant assessment event remains to be clarified. Assessment date must not silently become a universal implementation-date test.

Item (ii) expressly requires home-jurisdiction compliance. Item (i)'s separate home-supervision condition should not be imported automatically; the introductory description does not clearly establish an additional independent test.

Concrete classification requires applicable home-jurisdiction requirements and relevant SFC guidance on novelty, complexity and possible local policy implications. Those authorities are absent. Supplied classification inputs do not establish their own legal accuracy.

The external FAQs and forms/checklists are absent, and neither supplied unbound dependency ID is mapped to a named document. No mapping or contents are inferred. Their absence limits completeness review but does not prove an omitted executable condition.
Passing a substantive or proposed relief predicate does not establish legal approval, notification or filing compliance, post-vetting compliance, or the complete underlying prior-approval obligation.
